rows.quote: Here, we use an integrated multi-omics approach combining prospective cohort and exome-variant study designs to identify proteins with a role in cancer aetiology: we describe the association of 1463 protein biomarkers quantified using the Olink platform with the risk of 19 common cancers and 9 cancer subsites in 44,645 UK Biobank participants, overall and by time to diagnosis.
rows.coder_note: Step 3, rule C: the cancer outcomes are the authors' own analysis of UK Biobank individual-level data (application 67506), defined by a phenotype definition (19 cancers and 9 subsites) and an analysis procedure, not by a listed GWAS release; no accession (C4 not applicable).

rows.quote: Here, we use an integrated multi-omics approach combining prospective cohort and exome-variant study designs to identify proteins with a role in cancer aetiology: we describe the association of 1463 protein biomarkers quantified using the Olink platform with the risk of 19 common cancers and 9 cancer subsites in 44,645 UK Biobank participants, overall and by time to diagnosis.
rows.coder_note: Step 3, rule C: the protein data are the authors' own proteomic analysis of UK Biobank individual-level data (1463 Olink proteins in 44,645 participants, application 67506), defined by a measurement and analysis procedure. Step 2 does not apply: the exome pQTLs are attributed to Dhindsa et al. through entry 44, a bioRxiv preprint (DOI 10.1101/2022.10.09.511476v1) that is not the Dhindsa 2023 row's identifier, with 50,829 participants where that row has 49,736; the Sun 2023 citation (entry 38) is attached to sample selection and separates none of its four rows. No accession (C4 not applicable).
